draft.title: Neuromodulators
card: A neuromodulator is a chemical that changes how neurons respond to signals. It acts on many neurons at once, not just one.
acts on the one neuron across the synapse, to excite or inhibit it.
acts on a wider group of neurons. It adjusts how strongly they respond to other signals.
Dopamine is linked to reward and movement. Serotonin is linked to mood and sleep.
draft.remember: Neuromodulators adjust how whole groups of neurons respond. Dopamine: reward and movement. Serotonin: mood and sleep.

a.q: Which description best fits a neuromodulator?
opts: It changes how many neurons respond at the same time
It carries a signal across one synapse to a single neuron
It is a neuron that sends signals to a muscle
It is a part of the spinal cord that controls reflexes
a.why: A neuromodulator acts on many neurons at once and changes how they respond. Carrying a signal across one synapse to one neuron describes the action of a neurotransmitter, which is the tempting wrong option.
a.clue: Think about how many neurons it acts on.

b.q: Aiden has trouble getting to sleep and his mood has been low for weeks. Which neuromodulator is most closely linked to both sleep and mood?
opts: Serotonin
Dopamine
Glutamate
GABA
b.why: Serotonin is linked to mood and sleep. Dopamine is linked to reward and movement, so it is the tempting wrong option, but it is not the one tied to both of these.
b.clue: One neuromodulator covers both mood and sleep.

a.best: It changes how many neurons respond at the same time

problems.detail: The card defines neurotransmitters (acting on the one neuron across the synapse to excite or inhibit it), which is the idea of point 6. It should only mention neurotransmitters as a contrast, not explain them.

The right option, 'It changes how many neurons respond at the same time', can be misread as changing the number of neurons that respond. Clearer wording would be 'It acts on many neurons at once, changing how they respond'.

proposal.title: Neuromodulators
card: A neuromodulator is a chemical released by neurons. It changes how other neurons respond to the signals they receive.
It spreads out to act on many neurons at once. This sets it apart from a neurotransmitter, which works at a single synapse.
Its effects tend to be slower and last longer. It can turn the responses of a whole group of neurons up or down.
Dopamine is a neuromodulator linked to reward and movement. Serotonin is a neuromodulator linked to mood and sleep.
proposal.remember: Neuromodulators adjust many neurons at once. Dopamine: reward and movement. Serotonin: mood and sleep.

a.q: Which description best fits a neuromodulator?
opts: It acts on many neurons at once, changing how they respond
It works at a single synapse, passing a signal to one neuron
It is a neuron that carries a signal out to a muscle
It is a chemical made by a gland and carried in the blood
a.why: A neuromodulator is released by neurons and acts on many neurons at once, changing how they respond. Working at a single synapse is the tempting wrong option, but the card sets that apart as how a neurotransmitter works.
a.clue: Think about how many neurons it acts on.

b.q: Aiden has trouble getting to sleep and his mood has been low for weeks. Which neuromodulator is most closely linked to both sleep and mood?
opts: Serotonin
Dopamine
Glutamate
GABA
b.why: Serotonin is linked to mood and sleep. Dopamine is the tempting wrong option because it is also a neuromodulator, but it is linked to reward and movement instead.
b.clue: One neuromodulator covers both mood and sleep.
